choose_path.description:
Some locks mask stored PINs, making them invisible to external tools. Once LCM is managing your locks, do not set codes using other tools or manually at the lock. Clear all slots before setup. For permanent access codes, configure them through LCM without a condition entity.

Choose whether you want to configure each slot via the UI or if you want to configure all slots in a YAML config.

lock_offline.description: Lock Code Manager has been unable to communicate with `{lock_entity_id}` for multiple consecutive attempts. Code synchronization is paused until the lock is reachable again. This issue will be automatically dismissed when the lock recovers.

lock_setup_failed.title: Lock setup failed: {lock_entity_id}
lock_setup_failed.description:
Lock Code Manager could not set up `{lock_entity_id}`: {error}

Its entities are created but unavailable, and code synchronization is paused for this lock. After addressing the cause, reload the lock's integration (or Lock Code Manager) to retry. This issue will be automatically dismissed when setup succeeds.

lock_dropped.title: Lock dropped: {lock_entity_id}
lock_dropped.description:
Lock Code Manager could not create a provider for `{lock_entity_id}`, so it has been dropped from this configuration entry: {error}

No entities were created for that lock and no codes are written to it; every other lock in the entry is unaffected. This usually means the entity belongs to a bridge no Lock Code Manager provider supports, or that its integration has changed what it publishes about the device. Remove it from the entry, or fix the underlying cause and reload Lock Code Manager. This issue will be automatically dismissed once the lock sets up.

init.title: Unmanaged code on {lock} in slot {slot}
init.description:
Lock {lock} has a code programmed in slot {slot}, and no Lock Code Manager configuration accounts for it.

There are two ways this happens, and Lock Code Manager cannot tell them apart:

- Somebody programmed the code directly on the lock's keypad or in another app.
- Lock Code Manager left it behind. Before this version, deleting a user removed them from the configuration without clearing their code from the lock, so codes stranded that way are still there and still work.

Until this is settled, slot {slot} stays out of use: Lock Code Manager will not assign a new user to a slot it can still read a code in, because overwriting somebody's own code is the worse mistake.

**Clear the code** removes it from the lock. It stops working immediately and cannot be recovered — choose this only if you know nobody relies on it.

**Keep the code** leaves it exactly as it is and stops asking about this slot.

menu_options.keep: Keep the code and stop asking
